title: Harden PROJECT.md frontmatter: reject/escape control chars in project_name & project_type (YAML key injection)
description:
SECURITY — found by hive-adversarial-improve run against bin/init.js intake (probe P1/P2), verified by running the REAL runInit({answers}) end-to-end. src/project-md.js#renderProjectMd interpolates `name: ${name}` and `type: ${type}` into the YAML frontmatter with NO escaping/quoting and NO post-render re-validation. A newline in project_name therefore forges arbitrary top-level frontmatter keys, and readProjectMd restores them.

CONFIRMED live: project_name = "MyProj\nagent_models: {developer: opus, reviewer: haiku}\ntier: uat-only\nschema_version: 999\ninjected_name: PWNED" produced a PROJECT.md whose frontmatter carries a forged agent_models map + tier; readProjectMd returned frontmatter.agent_models={developer:opus,reviewer:haiku}, tier='uat-only'. IMPACT: `node bin/init.js --apply-models` reads agent_models from PROJECT.md and patches the reviewer/developer/researcher model frontmatter — so a forged project name can DOWNGRADE the independent review gate's model (e.g. reviewer inherit->haiku), bypassing writeProjectMd's agent_models validation (which only runs on answers.agent_models, never on content smuggled through name/type). Probe P2 (project_type containing `\n---\n...`) corroborates the same root cause: the injected `---` closes the frontmatter early, displacing created_at/schema_version into the body and letting the attacker forge a `## Description` — a document-integrity corruption from the same unescaped interpolation.

ROOT CAUSE: src/project-md.js:189-233 (renderProjectMd frontmatter lines) treat scalar values as trusted single-line strings. FIX DIRECTION (developer's choice): at the intake/write boundary, reject frontmatter scalar values that contain \r/\n (loud error naming the field) OR escape/quote them so read-back yields the literal string. Prefer a shared boundary sanitizer so this composes with the sibling tickets (Unicode-tag stripping, structural-forgery neutralization). Ensure created_at & schema_version always remain in the frontmatter block. tdd tier: this is parsing/schema-security logic.

FIXTURE: replay the exact P1 and P2 answer objects (documented above and in the session's probe harness scratchpad/probe-harness.mjs). Acceptance = replaying these inputs no longer injects any extra frontmatter key and never displaces the writer's own frontmatter fields.
acceptance_criteria: Replaying probe P1 (project_name with embedded newlines spelling `agent_models: {...}`, `tier:`, `schema_version:`, `injected_name:`) yields a PROJECT.md whose parsed frontmatter contains NO attacker-forged keys: readProjectMd returns exactly the writer's own keys (name, type, created_at, schema_version) plus only legitimately-supplied ones — no agent_models, no tier, no injected_name from the name field

The writer either rejects control characters (\r/\n) in project_name/project_type with a loud error that names the offending field BEFORE any disk write, or escapes/encodes them so readProjectMd round-trips the value as the exact literal string the caller supplied

Replaying probe P2 (project_type containing `
---
injected_key: ...
---`) never produces a PROJECT.md where the writer's own created_at/schema_version are displaced out of the frontmatter block, and no attacker-controlled `## Description` or `injected_key` appears from the type field

A red-first regression test replays P1 and P2 against the real writer/reader and asserts the injection is caught; it fails against current main for the right reason (shows the forged agent_models/tier) before the fix
Existing PROJECT.md round-trip tests still pass (legitimate project_name/project_type/agent_models/tier/perfil_proyecto values are unaffected)

comments.body: Closed on a clean first-pass APPROVE (review_depth: FULL; rubric inputs: security fix for a confirmed YAML-frontmatter key-injection vuln + parsing/schema logic in src/project-md.js + new e2e regression spec + committed dist rebuild — any one justifies full). Developer commit 0c1e8c0 (single tdd commit, tests+impl together): writeProjectMd now rejects \r/\n in project_name/project_type/tier with a loud field-naming error BEFORE any disk write (reject-over-escape, matching the module's strict-throw philosophy); tier folded in as same-class. New spec tests/e2e/project-md-frontmatter-injection.spec.js (5 tests) replays probes P1/P2 + tier variant + 2 legitimate-value sanity checks. Reviewer independently reproduced the tests-first red proof by reverse-applying ONLY the impl hunk (git apply -R) and re-running: 3 injection tests failed for the right reason (writeProjectMd silently wrote forged frontmatter), sanity tests stayed green (non-vacuous); then restored. Gate on committed diff: test:since -- 0c1e8c0~1 = 4 files/75 passed (non-vacuous, incl. injection spec); npm test = 977 passed/2 skip; dist-parity green (dist/init.cjs byte-fresh). Single chokepoint confirmed: renderProjectMd is private, both init paths converge on the one writeProjectMd call, no bypass. Findings: 0 HIGH in-scope, 1 MEDIUM (perfil_proyecto map values are the identical injection class, NOT covered by TASK-158's body/context scope — minted as dedicated follow-up TASK-161), 1 LOW (verbose comment, non-blocking). Knowledge capture (TASK-105) NOT triggered: no HIGH, zero RC loops. LOCAL/unpushed pending human push.
